Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
• 29-year-old man with 6-week history of generalized fatigue and diffuse musculoskeletal aches following U.S. hiking holiday; transient annular calf rash mid-Feb; clinical impression favors possible early Lyme disease.  

History:
• Presenting complaint: “aching all over” with marked tiredness/run-down feeling for ≈6 weeks.  
• Timeline: Well over Christmas/New Year; travelled to U.S. late Jan; symptoms began ≈2 wks after return (mid-Feb).  
   – Mid/late Feb: solitary, non-itchy erythematous rash on posterior calf lasting ~2 wks, associated with sore throat ± low-grade fever.  
• Associated symptoms: migratory aches (shoulders, back, hips, knees); mild non-specific headaches; reduced appetite; ↓ energy/concentration; no weight change.  
• Pertinent negatives: No persistent cough, dyspnea, GI/urinary changes, dysphagia, neurological deficits, joint swelling, additional rashes.  
• PMH: Asthma, hay fever.  
• Medications: Preventive inhaler (twice daily), OTC antihistamine.  
• Allergies: not documented.  
• Social / preventive: Enjoys hiking; wore shorts outdoors in U.S. (possible tick exposure). Lives with wife. Occasional alcohol; smoking status not clearly stated.  

Examination:
• No vitals or physical exam findings recorded during video consult.  
• Photograph reviewed: solitary annular lesion on calf (patient-reported).  

Impression:
• Most likely: Early disseminated Lyme disease (erythema migrans–like rash, outdoor exposure, subsequent fatigue/arthralgia).  
• Differential considerations:  
   – Post-viral fatigue (e.g., EBV/CMV) – sore throat, prolonged fatigue.  
   – Hypothyroidism – common cause of fatigue/myalgias; to be screened.  

Plan:
• Order blood panel: CBC, renal, liver, thyroid, inflammatory markers, iron/B12, viral serology as appropriate, and Lyme serology.  
• Patient to arrange phlebotomy via support line.  
• Follow-up: telephone review ~1 week after labs available.  
• If Lyme serology positive: initiate guideline-based antibiotic therapy (e.g., doxycycline).  
• Safety-net: advise patient to seek care sooner if fevers, neurologic symptoms, joint swelling, or worsening fatigue develop.  

Quality checks
● Missing/expected data: allergies, current smoking status, vitals, physical exam, family history, occupational exposures, formal medication list verification, planned antibiotic regimen details.  
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx: none noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear history; lacked vitals and physical exam; minor audio gaps but core information intact.
